newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama company to build hotel on former U.S. base.
newsitem.headline: Panama company to build hotel on former U.S. base.

text.p: Panama's leading construction company signed on Tuesday a 40-year concession deal to build a $9 million tourist complex on a former U.S. military base in Panama.

Grupo UNESA (Union Nacional de Empresas SA) will build a 250-room hotel with swimming pool and restaurant on Fort Amador, a former U.S. World War Two nerve center, UNESA president Guillermo Quijano Jr told a news conference.
He said a first phase of 100 rooms should be completed by the end of the year. Grupo UNESA has the option to renew for an additional 20 years.
The contract is the second agreement to build on Fort Amador.
A U.S.-Korean consortium, United Enterprise Trust Group, signed a deal last August to build a $300 million tourist resort, including a 500-room luxury hotel on an island off Fort Amador.
Located at the entrance of the Panama Canal on the Pacific side, Fort Amador was turned over to Panamanian control from the United States in October.
